children: Round-up of South Korean financial markets: ** South Korean shares fell on Monday after Anthropic and OpenAI called for a slowdown in artificial intelligence development. The won weakened, while the benchmark bond yield fell. ** The benchmark KOSPI
closed down 225.54 points, or 3.26%, at 6,684.37. ** Chipmaker Samsung Electronics

** Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called on AI companies to slow the pace of model development amid mounting fears of AI misuse, outlining a three-step framework to pace development and create more time to manage risks.

** Boston Dynamics, Hyundai Motor Group's humanoid robot unit, is unlikely to pursue an initial public offering next year, a senior executive at the parent company with direct knowledge of the matter said.

** Starting Monday, South Korea's main stock exchange, Korea Exchange, enabled after-hours trading from 4 p.m. to 8 p.m. local time, following a similar move by alternative trading system Nextrade, which introduced evening-hour trading in March 2025.  ** Among other index heavyweights, battery maker LG Energy Solution
were down 2.88% and down 1.90%, respectively. ** Steelmaker POSCO Holdings
rose 0.35%. ** Foreigners were net sellers of shares worth 3,288.0 billion won. ** The won was quoted at 1,346.8 per dollar on the onshore settlement platform

, 0.20% lower than its previous close at 1,344.1. ** The KOSPI has risen 58.62% so far this year. ** The won has strengthened 6.9% against the dollar so far this year. ** In money and debt markets, September futures on three-year treasury bonds (KTBc1) gained 0.03 point to 102.68. ** The most liquid three-year Korean treasury bond yield (KR3YT=RR) fell by 0.8 basis points to 4.015%, while the benchmark 10-year yield
